findings.title: get_monitor_environment_context modifies a local copy but returns the original config
findings.body: The function builds `config = monitor_environment.monitor.config.copy()` and mutates the local `config['schedule_type']` to its human-readable display value, but then the function returns `monitor_environment.monitor.config` (the original, unmodified dict) instead of the local `config`. As a result the `schedule_type` conversion is dead code, and any consumer of the `monitor` context (events produced to Kafka) will receive the raw stored value (e.g. `"crontab"`) rather than the display value (e.g. `"Crontab"`).

findings.title: Docstring typo and inaccurate singular example in get_failure_reason
findings.body: The docstring contains the typo "humam readible" (should be "human readable") and the third example "A failed check-in was detected" does not match what the code actually produces for a single failing check-in. The real singular messages in SINGULAR_HUMAN_FAILURE_MAP are "An error check-in was detected", "A missed check-in was detected", and "A timeout check-in was detected".

findings.title: Public SimpleCheckIn TypedDict moved, breaking any existing import path
findings.body: Previously `SimpleCheckIn` was defined in `sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed`; it has been removed from that module and re-defined in `sentry.monitors.types`. Any external caller doing `from sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed import SimpleCheckIn` (or importing it transitively) will now hit an ImportError. Because the type is part of a function signature in the public API of this module, it should either be re-exported from `mark_failed.py` for backwards compatibility, or the rename should be called out explicitly in the PR description / changelog.

findings.title: Renamed helper functions leave existing tests referencing the old names
findings.body: `mark_failed_threshold` was renamed to `try_incident_threshold` and `create_issue_platform_occurrence` was renamed to `create_incident_occurrence`, but no test file was updated in this PR. Any test that imports these symbols by their previous names (or that patches them via `mock.patch`) will fail to collect/run. The refactor needs an accompanying test update (rename references, adjust patch targets) and ideally a test that exercises the new module layout end-to-end.

findings.title: Unused module-level logger in new modules
findings.body: Both `incidents.py` (line 11) and `incident_occurrence.py` (line 25) define `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` but neither file emits any log records. Either drop the unused logger or add the intended log statements; leaving it in just adds noise and a misleading signal that logging happens here.

findings.title: monitor_env.get_environment() called twice per occurrence, in a loop
findings.body: Inside `create_incident_occurrence`, `monitor_env.get_environment().name` is accessed on line 67 (evidence display) and again on line 90 (`event_data["environment"]`). `incidents.try_incident_threshold` then calls `create_incident_occurrence` once for every check-in in `previous_checkins`, so the environment lookup (typically a DB query on `Environment`) is performed 2 * len(previous_checkins) times per failing check-in. The environment should be resolved once at the top of `create_incident_occurrence` and reused.
